sent_to_model:
I'd like help writing a review of Heimat 2 alongside other viewers' comments. Other people have already covered a lot of the series and praised its historical and artistic range. I first watched it at art college, among artists and musicians hoping to make something of ourselves, and it really mattered to me. Please explain that personal connection and why the music and performers have stayed with me. I'd also like to argue for its place alongside great cinema and television: I admire other ambitious series, but this one deserves much more recognition. Please mention that I still go back to it every autumn.

- Henry Arnold plays Hermann; piano.
- First viewing: BBC2 in the 1990s, over seventeen years before writing.
- Other admired television creators: Dennis Potter and David Lynch.
- Had seen neither Heimat nor Heimat 3; watched Heimat 2 independently.
- Composer Nikos Mamangakis studied with Carl Orff, composer of Carmina Burana.
- At art college, spent time among musicians and artists with professional ambitions.
- Gisela Muller plays Evelyn; singing.
- Rewatch the three boxed sets every autumn.
- Series includes friendships after leaving family and striving for artistic achievement.
- Salome Kammer plays Clarissa; cello.
- Other comments have discussed historical scale and artistry.
- Daniel Smith plays Juan; Bach on marimba.
- The Wire comparison topics: city life, politics, realism.
- Photography and storytelling captivating.
- Musical associations: 1970s Can, Faust, Kraftwerk and Neue; 1950s Stockhausen.
- All four named performers' musical moments are favourites.
- Series neglected in critics' best-film selections.
- Additional score associations: sound effects, electronic pop.
- As powerful and inspiring now as at first viewing.
- Further musical associations: The White Noise, Walter Carlos, John Cage.
- Art-college friendships and ambitions made series personally important.
- Autumn feels suited to rewatching.
- Historical and artistic scope impressive.

(About me: viewer who attended art college. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Explain the connection between the art-college viewing experience and the series' friendships and artistic ambitions.
Describe the lasting appeal of the music and performers.
Argue for greater recognition alongside great cinema and television.
